reasoning: Both pass the behaviour check and both keep the bare return in getTallest. A has clean tooling and a shared filter, but it keeps the numeric-Type crash in summarize, doesn't handle a missing price, and changes the error-message format. B fixes the data-shape bug where it matters and types the price lookup as optional; its one-line StyLua failure is trivial to fix. B wins narrowly.

criteria.note: Lune parity passes; swapping assert for error() adds a position prefix to the error message, and the numeric-Type crash in summarize is kept.
Names are spelled out, guard via a shared isCountedBlock filter, and constants such as BLOCK_HALF_HEIGHT, BULK_DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD and POINTS_PER_* are named.
formatWholeNumber and formatOneDecimal are local functions; no positional booleans are left.
Splits BLOCK_COST and BLOCK_TYPES, but isCountedBlock still accepts BLOCK_TYPES[blockType], so summarize still errors on a numeric Type (documented).
Strict and typed, but `cost += BLOCK_COST[blockType]` has no optional handling, and getTallest keeps a bare `return`.
Only PlotStats changed; luau-lsp, selene and StyLua all pass; comments are accurate.
Lune parity passes; keeps assert with the same message; only the former crash case in summarize changes, to a skip.
Constants are well named and guard clauses are used, but summarize and getTallest each check blocks separately instead of sharing a filter.
formatWholeNumber, formatOneDecimal and pluralize are local functions.
BLOCK_TYPES records plus a derived COST_BY_TYPE map; summarize skips a numeric Type through the blockCost nil check, and the quirk stays only in getTallest.
Optional Block fields and an explicit check on blockCost; a bare `return` is still left in getTallest.
Only PlotStats changed, but StyLua fails on its own single-line assert.

weaknesses: Keeps the numeric-Type crash in summarize
Price lookup isn't typed as optional
error() changes the assert message format
BLOCK_TYPES built from a dictionary loop, so its order isn't fixed
